data.name: Plum
data.about:
Food delivery for one city. Customers order in the app or on the website, restaurants cook, couriers deliver.

Start with **Ordering**, which every order passes through. **Delivery** covers courier matching and tracking.

customer.name: Customer
customer.description: Orders from the Plum app or the website.

restaurant.name: Restaurant
restaurant.description: Kitchen staff. Accept orders and mark them ready.

courier.name: Courier
courier.description: Carries the order from the restaurant to the customer's door.

ordering.name: Ordering
ordering.description:
Everything customer-facing: menus, basket, payment.

The **Order API** is the only entry point. It stores orders in Postgres and publishes each
new order to **Order events**, which **Delivery** consumes.

delivery.name: Delivery
delivery.description:
Assigns a courier to each order and tracks it to the door.

Dispatch matches and offers. Live tracking feeds the customer's map.

notifications.name: Notifications
notifications.description: Push, SMS and email. The only system that talks to a messaging provider.

backoffice.name: Back office
backoffice.description: Internal tools for Plum staff. Not exposed to customers or couriers.

stripe.name: Stripe
stripe.description: Card payments and refunds. Plum never handles card numbers.

customer-app.name: Customer app
customer-app.description:
Mobile client. Browse, order, pay, follow the courier.

Stores only the basket and the session.

web.name: Website
web.description: The same ordering flow in a browser. Menus are server-rendered so search engines can index them.

kitchen-tablet.name: Kitchen tablet
kitchen-tablet.description: Alerts on a new order. The kitchen taps **Accept**, then **Ready** for pickup.

order-api.name: Order API
order-api.description:
Entry point for every client, and the only service that touches the **Orders DB**.

- `GET /menus/:restaurant` reads a menu
- `POST /orders` places an order
- `POST /orders/:id/refund` refunds one

orders-db.name: Orders DB
orders-db.description: Orders, baskets and refunds. The source of truth for what a customer owes and was charged.

data.name: orders
data.note: One row per order. A refund adds a row to refunds and leaves the order alone.

columns.name: total
columns.note: Stored in cents because rounding broke the first tax run.

columns.name: unit_price
columns.note: Copied from the menu at order time. Later menu edits don't change it.

menu-cache.name: Menu cache
menu-cache.description: Menus, 5 min TTL. A restaurant's edit appears when the entry expires.

data.name: Keys
data.note: 5 min TTL. A shorter one put too much load on Postgres.

events.name: Order events
events.description:
One message per order change: `placed`, `accepted`, `picked-up`, `delivered`.

Dispatch and the warehouse are consumers.

data.name: order-events
data.note: Keyed by order id, so each order's messages stay ordered.

menu.name: Menu
menu.description: Serves menus from the cache, and from the database on a miss.

basket.name: Basket
basket.description: Holds the picked items and asks **Pricing** for the running total.

pricing.name: Pricing
pricing.description:
Computes the total: items, delivery fee and any promotion.

The fee is based on Mapbox travel distance, rounded up to the next 500 m.

snippets.title: Delivery fee

checkout.name: Checkout
checkout.description:
Prices the basket, authorises the card and places the order.

The card is charged only when the restaurant accepts. A rejection releases the hold.

status.name: Order status
status.description: Advances an order through `placed`, `accepted`, `picked-up` and `delivered`, publishing each step.

snippets.title: Accepting an order
snippets.text:
UPDATE orders
SET status = 'accepted', updated_at = now()
WHERE id = $1 AND status = 'placed'

refunds.name: Refunds
refunds.description: Refunds the card, then marks the order refunded. Full or per line.

courier-app.name: Courier app
courier-app.description: Offers, navigation and proof of delivery. Reports position every 5 s while a job is open.

dispatch.name: Dispatch
dispatch.description:
Assigns a courier to each new order.

Consumes `placed` events and offers the job to couriers one at a time, nearest first.

tracking.name: Live tracking
tracking.description: Relays courier position to the customer's map. Positions older than 1 min are dropped.

fleet-db.name: Fleet DB
fleet-db.description: Couriers, vehicles and last known position.

matcher.name: Matcher
matcher.description: Ranks idle couriers near a restaurant by estimated arrival.

eta.name: ETA
eta.description: Estimates travel time from distance, traffic and vehicle.

offers.name: Offers
offers.description:
Offers the job to one courier at a time with a 30 s timeout.

A refusal or timeout moves to the next courier.

notifier.name: Notifier
notifier.description: Chooses push, SMS or email per message and sends it. Never blocks the caller.

admin.name: Admin dashboard

files.text:
name: Plum
about: |
  Food delivery for one city. Customers order in the app or on the website, restaurants cook, couriers deliver.

  Start with **Ordering**, which every order passes through. **Delivery** covers courier matching and tracking.
objects:
  customer:
    type: actor
    name: Customer
    description: Orders from the Plum app or the website.
  restaurant:
    type: actor
    name: Restaurant
    description: Kitchen staff. Accept orders and mark them ready.
  courier:
    type: actor
    name: Courier
    icon: truck
    description: Carries the order from the restaurant to the customer's door.
  support:
    type: actor
    name: Support agent
    description: Answers customer and courier tickets.
  ordering:
    type: system
    name: Ordering
    description: |
      Everything customer-facing: menus, basket, payment.

      The **Order API** is the only entry point. It stores orders in Postgres and publishes each
      new order to **Order events**, which **Delivery** consumes.
  delivery:
    type: system
    name: Delivery
    description: |
      Assigns a courier to each order and tracks it to the door.

      Dispatch matches and offers. Live tracking feeds the customer's map.
  notifications:
    type: system
    name: Notifications
    description: Push, SMS and email. The only system that talks to a messaging provider.
  backoffice:
    type: system
    name: Back office
    description: Internal tools for Plum staff. Not exposed to customers or couriers.
  stripe:
    type: system
    name: Stripe
    external: true
    description: Card payments and refunds. Plum never handles card numbers.
    links:
      - url: https://status.stripe.com
        title: Provider status
  twilio:
    type: system
    name: Twilio
    external: true
    description: SMS delivery.
  mapbox:
    type: system
    name: Mapbox
    external: true
    description: Maps, geocoding and travel times.
    links:
      - url: https://docs.mapbox.com/api/overview/#rate-limits
        title: Rate limits
  customer-app:
    type: app
    in: ordering
    name: Customer app
    tech: React Native
    code:
      - apps/customer/
    links:
      - url: apps/customer/README.md
        title: Build and release notes
    description: |
      Mobile client. Browse, order, pay, follow the courier.

      Stores only the basket and the session.
  web:
    type: app
    in: ordering
    name: Website
    tech: Next.js
    description: The same ordering flow in a browser. Menus are server-rendered so search engines can index them.
  kitchen-tablet:
    type: app
    in: ordering
    name: Kitchen tablet
    tech: Android
    description: Alerts on a new order. The kitchen taps **Accept**, then **Ready** for pickup.
  order-api:
    type: app
    in: ordering
    name: Order API
    tech: Node, Fastify
    code:
      - services/order-api/
    description: |
      Entry point for every client, and the only service that touches the **Orders DB**.

      - `GET /menus/:restaurant` reads a menu
      - `POST /orders` places an order
      - `POST /orders/:id/refund` refunds one
  orders-db:
    type: store
    in: ordering
    name: Orders DB
    tech: Postgres
    description: Orders, baskets and refunds. The source of truth for what a customer owes and was charged.
    data:
      - name: orders
        kind: table
        limits: Kept 7 years, then archived
        note: One row per order. A refund adds a row to refunds and leaves the order alone.
        columns:
          - {name: id, type: uuid, key: primary}
          - {name: customer_id, type: uuid, to: customers}
          - {name: total, type: int, note: Stored in cents because rounding broke the first tax run.}
        rows:
          - [o_1042, c_77, 2490]
          - [o_1043, c_12, 1380]
          - [o_1044, c_77, 990]
      - name: order_items
        columns:
          - {name: order_id, type: uuid, key: primary, to: orders}
          - {name: item_id, type: uuid, key: primary}
          - {name: quantity, type: int}
          - {name: unit_price, type: int, note: Copied from the menu at order time. Later menu edits don't change it.}
        rows:
          - [o_1042, i_31, 2, 1245]
          - [o_1043, i_8, 1, 1380]
      - name: refunds
        limits: Kept with its order
        columns:
          - {name: id, type: uuid, key: primary}
          - {name: order_id, type: uuid, to: orders}
          - {name: amount, type: int}
          - {name: reason, type: text?}
        rows:
          - [r_9, o_1044, 990, Wrong item]
      - name: baskets
        limits: Swept after 24 hours
        columns:
          - {name: id, type: uuid, key: primary}
          - {name: customer_id, type: uuid, to: customers}
          - {name: items, type: json}
          - {name: expires_at, type: timestamp}
  menu-cache:
    type: store
    in: ordering
    name: Menu cache
    tech: Redis
    description: Menus, 5 min TTL. A restaurant's edit appears when the entry expires.
    data:
      - name: Keys
        limits: LRU eviction at 256 MB
        note: 5 min TTL. A shorter one put too much load on Postgres.
        columns: [Key, Value, Expires]
        rows:
          - ["menu:{restaurantId}", "{ items, prices, hours }", 5 min]
          - [menu:r_42, '{ "items": 31 }', 3 min left]
  events:
    type: store
    in: ordering
    name: Order events
    shape: queue
    tech: Kafka
    description: |
      One message per order change: `placed`, `accepted`, `picked-up`, `delivered`.

      Dispatch and the warehouse are consumers.
    data:
      - name: order-events
        kind: topic
        limits: Kept 7 days, 6 partitions
        note: Keyed by order id, so each order's messages stay ordered.
        columns: [Key, Value]
        rows:
          - [o_1042, '{ "type": "placed", "total": 2490 }']
          - [o_1042, '{ "type": "accepted" }']
          - [o_1042, '{ "type": "picked-up" }']
  menu:
    type: component
    in: order-api
    name: Menu
    description: Serves menus from the cache, and from the database on a miss.
  basket:
    type: component
    in: order-api
    name: Basket
    description: Holds the picked items and asks **Pricing** for the running total.
  pricing:
    type: component
    in: order-api
    name: Pricing
    code:
      - services/order-api/src/pricing.ts
    description: |
      Computes the total: items, delivery fee and any promotion.

      The fee is based on Mapbox travel distance, rounded up to the next 500 m.
    snippets:
      - title: Delivery fee
        language: typescript
        text: |-
          // Mapbox answers in metres. Round up to the next 500 m.
          const km = Math.ceil(meters / 500) / 2
          const fee = Math.max(MIN_FEE, BASE_FEE + km * PER_KM)
  checkout:
    type: component
    in: order-api
    name: Checkout
    code:
      - services/order-api/src/checkout.ts
    description: |
      Prices the basket, authorises the card and places the order.

      The card is charged only when the restaurant accepts. A rejection releases the hold.
  status:
    type: component
    in: order-api
    name: Order status
    description: Advances an order through `placed`, `accepted`, `picked-up` and `delivered`, publishing each step.
    snippets:
      - title: Accepting an order
        text: |-
          UPDATE orders
          SET status = 'accepted', updated_at = now()
          WHERE id = $1 AND status = 'placed'
  refunds:
    type: component
    in: order-api
    name: Refunds
    description: Refunds the card, then marks the order refunded. Full or per line.
  courier-app:
    type: app
    in: delivery
    name: Courier app
    tech: Kotlin, Swift
    description: Offers, navigation and proof of delivery. Reports position every 5 s while a job is open.
  dispatch:
    type: app
    in: delivery
    name: Dispatch
    tech: Go
    code:
      - services/dispatch/
    description: |
      Assigns a courier to each new order.

      Consumes `placed` events and offers the job to couriers one at a time, nearest first.
  tracking:
    type: app
    in: delivery
    name: Live tracking
    tech: Go, WebSocket
    description: Relays courier position to the customer's map. Positions older than 1 min are dropped.
  fleet-db:
    type: store
    in: delivery
    name: Fleet DB
    tech: Postgres, PostGIS
    description: Couriers, vehicles and last known position.
  matcher:
    type: component
    in: dispatch
    name: Matcher
    code:
      - services/dispatch/matcher.go
    description: Ranks idle couriers near a restaurant by estimated arrival.
  eta:
    type: component
    in: dispatch
    name: ETA
    description: Estimates travel time from distance, traffic and vehicle.
  offers:
    type: component
    in: dispatch
    name: Offers
    description: |
      Offers the job to one courier at a time with a 30 s timeout.

      A refusal or timeout moves to the next courier.
  notifier:
    type: app
    in: notifications
    name: Notifier
    tech: Node
    description: Chooses push, SMS or email per message and sends it. Never blocks the caller.
  templates:
    type: store
    in: notifications
    name: Message templates
    shape: document
    tech: Postgres
    description: Message text, per language.
  admin:
    type: app
    in: backoffice
    name: Admin dashboard
    tech: React
    description: Restaurants, delivery zones, promotions and the weekly reports.
  support-console:
    type: app
    in: backoffice
    name: Support console
    tech: React
    description: Look up an order, see where the courier is, issue a refund.
  warehouse:
    type: store
    in: backoffice
    name: Data warehouse
    tech: ClickHouse
    description: Every order event, kept for reporting. Only the **Admin dashboard** reads it.

steps.name: Step animations
steps.description:
One pair of shapes for each way a step can travel, named for the animation they play.

Each animation has a flow of its own with a single step to click through: Send, Call, Event, Callback, Flash, Bolt drop,
Send with a word, Fail, Timeout, Lost, Rejected, Intercepted (twice: by a shape and by a name), Duplicated, Delayed and Share
(Flash has two, because the step before sets it off).

**Every step animation** plays them all: press **P** to watch them one after the other.

structure.name: Flow structure
structure.description:
One set of shapes for each way steps can be grouped: **Repeat**, **Branch**, **Parallel** and **Flow link**.

Each has a flow of the same name, with the chip, lane tabs and progress bar that go with it.

performance.name: Performance
performance.description:
One shape for each thing a load test can show, named for what it shows.

Open the Performance tab (**T**), pick **Every load effect**, then press **Ramp** or step the levels with the arrow keys.

states.name: Shape states
states.description:
One shape that goes through every state, and one that holds another shape in a state.

Play **Every state** to watch a shape start, run, degrade, stop, restart and run again, and **State inside a shape** to see a shape show that something inside it is not running.

time.name: Runs over time
time.description:
A run measured over time instead of over load, with events on its timeline that set the state of a shape.

Open the Performance tab (**T**), pick **Every state over time**, then press **Play**, drag the slider or click an event.

compare.name: Compare
compare.description:
A flow and the flow that replaced it, tagged as a pair, with a note. Each has one step that goes, one that is new and one that changes, so every mark is on show.

Play **Compare after** and press **C** to open the pair. Turn on **Show changes** for the marks, and pick **Swap** then **X** to watch the shapes glide, fade in and fade out.

send-from.name: Send · from
send-from.description: `animation: send`. Something runs one way along the line. The sender does not wait.

send-to.name: Send · to
send-to.description: Takes the envelope in with a squash.

effects-from.name: Effects · from
effects-from.description: `animation: { kind: send, effect: bounce }`. What the moving label does on its way, besides travelling. None of them bends its shape.

effects-to.name: Effects · to
effects-to.description: Sits down the slope from its sender, so the label runs along a slanted line and shows it stays level.

call-from.name: Call · from
call-from.description: `animation: call`. The envelope goes, the sender waits, and the reply comes back.

call-to.name: Call · to
call-to.description: Takes the envelope in, then answers.

event-from.name: Event · from
event-from.description: `animation: event`. A bolt runs along the line, and the receiver flashes.

callback-from.name: Callback · from
callback-from.description: `animation: callback`. A ring leaves this shape and a bell runs to the subscriber.

callback-to.name: Callback · to
callback-to.description: The subscriber. A ring goes out when the bell arrives.

after-source.name: Flash · source
after-source.description: Hands something to the publisher, which is what sets the callback off.

after-from.name: Flash · from
after-from.description: `animation: {kind: callback, trigger: outside}`, right after a step that landed here. This shape flashes, then the bell runs.

cold-from.name: Bolt drop · from
cold-from.description: `animation: {kind: callback, trigger: outside}`, with no step before it that landed here. A bolt drops onto this shape, then the bell runs.

fail-from.name: Fail · from
fail-from.description: `animation: {kind: send, outcome: fail}`. The envelope runs to the receiver, which refuses it.

timeout-from.name: Timeout · from
timeout-from.description: `animation: {kind: call, outcome: timeout}`. The envelope goes, the sender waits, no reply comes, and the line dims.

timeout-to.name: Timeout · to
timeout-to.description: Takes the envelope in and never answers.

lost-from.name: Lost · from
lost-from.description: `animation: {kind: send, outcome: lost, reason: Packet dropped}`. The envelope runs part of the way, pops, and leaves a cross where it went.

lost-to.name: Lost · to
lost-to.description: Never hears of it, so it never squashes or flashes.

rejected-from.name: Rejected · from
rejected-from.description: `animation: {kind: call, outcome: rejected, reason: Rate limit}`. The envelope stops at the bar by the receiver and comes back red.

rejected-to.name: Rejected · to
rejected-to.description: Turns the call away at the door. The bar flashes.

intercepted-from.name: Intercepted · from
intercepted-from.description: `animation: {kind: call, outcome: intercepted, by: intercepted-by}`. The envelope leaves the line for a third shape, which takes it and lights.

intercepted-by.name: Intercepted · taken by
intercepted-by.tech: not an end of the step
intercepted-by.description: The third shape. It gets a dashed outline for the whole step and lights when the envelope arrives.

named-from.name: Intercepted by a name · from
named-from.description: `animation: {kind: call, outcome: intercepted, by: {name: Café wifi proxy}}`. The party is not in the model, so a dashed marker with its name hangs below the line.

duplicated-from.name: Duplicated · from
duplicated-from.description: `animation: {kind: send, outcome: duplicated, reason: Retried}`. A second copy leaves the first part of the way along and arrives later.

duplicated-to.name: Duplicated · to
duplicated-to.description: Takes the envelope in twice, with a squash each time.

delayed-from.name: Delayed · from
delayed-from.description: `animation: {kind: call, outcome: delayed, reason: Cold start}`. The envelope waits partway beside a turning dashed clock, then goes on.

delayed-to.name: Delayed · to
delayed-to.description: Takes the envelope in late, then answers.

share-from.name: Share of requests · from
share-from.description: `animation: {kind: send, outcome: lost, share: 30, at: 0.7}`. Ten requests go one after another and three of them are lost 70 percent of the way along: r1, r2 and r3, each with its own colour and a ring.

share-to.name: Share of requests · to
share-to.description: Takes in the seven that arrive.

repeat-from.name: Repeat · from
repeat-from.description: The caller. It asks again until the service answers.

repeat-to.name: Repeat · to
repeat-to.description: The service. It is busy on the first two tries.

parallel-a.name: Parallel · lane A
parallel-a.description: Has two steps, so lane A keeps going after the others have finished.

link-from.name: Flow link · from
link-from.description: Hands the story to another flow.

link-to.name: Flow link · to
link-to.description: Where the other flow carries on.

load.name: Load
load.description: Where the load comes in. Every shape below is reached from here.

traffic.name: Traffic
traffic.description: The line from Load gets thicker and busier as the load goes up. The shape itself stays plain.

latency.name: Latency
latency.description: The dots on the line from Load slow down as calls take longer. The shape itself stays plain.

failing-calls.name: Failing calls
failing-calls.description: More and more of the dots on the line from Load turn red. The shape itself stays plain.

strain.name: Strain
strain.description: Busy. The outline runs from green to red as the shape uses more of its capacity, from 10% at 10 requests/s to 100% at 160.

failing-shape.name: Failing shape
failing-shape.description: Busy because calls fail. Failing 5% counts as full, so the outline runs to red early.

queue.name: Queue
queue.description: Waiting. The number is how many calls are waiting, from 0 to 3000. The outline stays plain because only the waiting was measured.

not-measured.name: Not measured
not-measured.description: Nothing was measured here, so it stays plain at every load. Missing is never drawn as zero.

rolled-up.name: Rolled up
rolled-up.description:
A shape that holds others shows the worst strain inside it and the waiting added up.

Double-click it to see each part.

rolled-a.name: Rolled up · A
rolled-a.description: Busy and waiting both grow. At 10 requests/s it is 20% busy with nothing waiting, and at 160 it is 90% busy with 120 waiting.

rolled-b.name: Rolled up · B
rolled-b.description: Waits for 10 calls at every load, and gets less busy as the load goes up, from 50% to 30%.

states-caller.name: State · caller
states-caller.description: Calls the other shapes. It is always running.

states-service.name: State · service
states-service.description: Goes through every state, one step at a time.

states-holder.name: State · holder
states-holder.description: Holds a part. Shows a ring with a dashed edge while the part is in a state and it has none of its own.

states-part.name: State · part
states-part.description: The part. Its state shows on the holder at the overview.

time-caller.name: Time · caller
time-caller.description: Calls the other shapes. It is always running, and gets busy while the service is off.

time-service.name: Time · service
time-service.description: Goes through every state as the run plays, one event at a time.

time-holder.name: Time · holder
time-holder.description: Holds a part. Shows a ring with a dashed edge while the part is in a state and it has none of its own.

time-part.name: Time · part
time-part.description: The part. It stops at 45 s and runs again at 72 s, and its state shows on the holder at the overview.

scale.name: Colour and scale
scale.description:
One shape for each thing a run's **source** sets: the colour of the dots, how many dots stand for the calls, and how big each is.

Open the Performance tab (**T**), pick **Colour and scale**, then press **Ramp** or step the levels with the arrow keys.

source.name: Source
source.description: Where the calls come in. Every dot on the lines from here is blue, because the run sets a colour.

dots-few.name: Few calls
dots-few.description: One dot for every 50 calls a second. The line goes from 50 calls a second to 800, so from 1 dot to 16.

dots-many.name: Ten times the calls
dots-many.description: Ten times the calls of Few calls, so ten times the dots, until the screen limit. Past 24 dots at once the line is scaled down, and the key and its numbers say so.

dots-slow.name: Same calls, slower
dots-slow.description: The same calls as Few calls, so the same number of dots, but each call takes longer, so the dots move slower.

dots-big.name: Bigger calls
dots-big.description: The more bytes a call carries, the bigger its dot. The area of a dot follows the size of a call, so 1,600 bytes is a dot twice as wide as 400 bytes.

calls-lost.name: Lost calls
calls-lost.description: A share of the calls dies on the way. Each ends in a small pop where it is lost.

calls-rejected.name: Rejected calls
calls-rejected.description: A share of the calls is turned away at the end of the line. Each stops at a bar and comes back red.

sources.name: Several sources
sources.description:
Two sources of requests at once, each with its own slider, colour and scale: added from separate runs (**Several sources added**) and tested together (**Several sources tested together**).

Open the Performance tab (**T**), pick one of them, then move a slider or press **Ramp** on a source. The chart follows the source you moved last.

a-in.name: Source A
a-in.description: Where Source A's calls come in. Its dots are blue, one for every 50 calls a second, and bigger than Source B's because its calls carry more.

b-in.name: Source B
b-in.description: Where Source B's calls come in. Its dots are green, one for every 10 calls a second.

gateway.name: Where they meet
gateway.description: Both sources send their calls through here. The line to Shared service carries both, so it has a stream of dots for each, side by side, in its colour. Past 24 dots at once both are scaled down together, so the ratio stays true.

shared.name: Shared service
shared.description: Both sources fill it. In the run added from separate runs its use is the two added, and past 100% it reads "Added use is over 100%". In the run tested together it is what was measured with both at once.

audit.name: Not split by source
audit.description: The run says how many calls this line carries but not which source sent them, so its dots are grey and the key says "Other calls".

compare-client.name: Compare · client
compare-client.description: Both flows start here, with the same first step, so it carries no mark.

compare-api.name: Compare · api
compare-api.description: Used by every step of both flows. A shape both flows draw is Changed when a step on it is marked.

compare-old.name: Compare · old service
compare-old.description: Only the older flow calls it, so it is Removed.

compare-db.name: Compare · database
compare-db.description: Both flows read it, but the newer one waits for the answer, so its step and line are Changed.

compare-cache.name: Compare · cache
compare-cache.description: Only the newer flow calls it, so it is New.

channels.name: Open channels
channels.description:
Three things a step can leave open for the steps after it: an **Open stream**, **Listening** and a **Running job**.

Play **Every open channel**: each one stays drawn until a step closes it, so you can see it keep running while the story moves on.

chan-client.name: Channels · client
chan-client.description: Opens a stream, registers a listener and starts a job, then closes each one.

chan-feed.name: Channels · feed
chan-feed.description: `opens: stream`. Dots keep running along the line, towards the client, until a step closes it.

chan-hook.name: Channels · webhook
chan-hook.description: `opens: listener`. A bell rings out from the client, which keeps listening for what the webhook sends.

chan-worker.name: Channels · worker
chan-worker.description: `opens: job`. An arc keeps turning on the worker while the job runs.

  scale:
    type: system
    name: Colour and scale
    description: |
      One shape for each thing a run's **source** sets: the colour of the dots, how many dots stand for the calls, and how big each is.

      Open the Performance tab (**T**), pick **Colour and scale**, then press **Ramp** or step the levels with the arrow keys.
  source:
    type: app
    in: scale
    name: Source
    description: Where the calls come in. Every dot on the lines from here is blue, because the run sets a colour.
  dots-few:
    type: app
    in: scale
    name: Few calls
    description: One dot for every 50 calls a second. The line goes from 50 calls a second to 800, so from 1 dot to 16.
  dots-many:
    type: app
    in: scale
    name: Ten times the calls
    description: Ten times the calls of Few calls, so ten times the dots, until the screen limit. Past 24 dots at once the line is scaled down, and the key and its numbers say so.
  dots-slow:
    type: app
    in: scale
    name: Same calls, slower
    description: The same calls as Few calls, so the same number of dots, but each call takes longer, so the dots move slower.
  dots-big:
    type: app
    in: scale
    name: Bigger calls
    description: The more bytes a call carries, the bigger its dot. The area of a dot follows the size of a call, so 1,600 bytes is a dot twice as wide as 400 bytes.
  calls-lost:
    type: app
    in: scale
    name: Lost calls
    description: A share of the calls dies on the way. Each ends in a small pop where it is lost.
  calls-rejected:
    type: app
    in: scale
    name: Rejected calls
    description: A share of the calls is turned away at the end of the line. Each stops at a bar and comes back red.
  sources:
    type: system
    name: Several sources
    description: |
      Two sources of requests at once, each with its own slider, colour and scale: added from separate runs (**Several sources added**) and tested together (**Several sources tested together**).

      Open the Performance tab (**T**), pick one of them, then move a slider or press **Ramp** on a source. The chart follows the source you moved last.
  a-in:
    type: app
    in: sources
    name: Source A
    description: Where Source A's calls come in. Its dots are blue, one for every 50 calls a second, and bigger than Source B's because its calls carry more.
  b-in:
    type: app
    in: sources
    name: Source B
    description: Where Source B's calls come in. Its dots are green, one for every 10 calls a second.
  gateway:
    type: app
    in: sources
    name: Where they meet
    description: Both sources send their calls through here. The line to Shared service carries both, so it has a stream of dots for each, side by side, in its colour. Past 24 dots at once both are scaled down together, so the ratio stays true.
  shared:
    type: store
    in: sources
    name: Shared service
    description: Both sources fill it. In the run added from separate runs its use is the two added, and past 100% it reads "Added use is over 100%". In the run tested together it is what was measured with both at once.
  audit:
    type: app
    in: sources
    name: Not split by source
    description: The run says how many calls this line carries but not which source sent them, so its dots are grey and the key says "Other calls".
  compare-client:
    type: app
    in: compare
    name: Compare · client
    description: Both flows start here, with the same first step, so it carries no mark.
  compare-api:
    type: app
    in: compare
    name: Compare · api
    description: Used by every step of both flows. A shape both flows draw is Changed when a step on it is marked.
  compare-old:
    type: app
    in: compare
    name: Compare · old service
    description: Only the older flow calls it, so it is Removed.
  compare-db:
    type: store
    in: compare
    name: Compare · database
    description: Both flows read it, but the newer one waits for the answer, so its step and line are Changed.
  compare-cache:
    type: store
    in: compare
    name: Compare · cache
    description: Only the newer flow calls it, so it is New.
  channels:
    type: system
    name: Open channels
    description: |
      Three things a step can leave open for the steps after it: an **Open stream**, **Listening** and a **Running job**.

      Play **Every open channel**: each one stays drawn until a step closes it, so you can see it keep running while the story moves on.
  chan-client:
    type: app
    in: channels
    name: Channels · client
    tech: opens and closes
    description: Opens a stream, registers a listener and starts a job, then closes each one.
  chan-feed:

  chan-worker:

    name: Channels · worker
    tech: job
    description: "`opens: job`. An arc keeps turning on the worker while the job runs."
